title: Look up optional values with map, flatMap and a lazy default

blocks.text: `Optional`'s methods take functional interfaces, so method references fit them: `map(String::length)`, `filter(...)`, `ifPresent(...)`. A reference that itself returns an `Optional` belongs in `flatMap`, or the result nests as `Optional<Optional<T>>`. A `Supplier` such as `ArrayList::new` defers its work until `get()` is called.
`Member` is a record `(String name, String nick)` whose `nickname()` method returns `Optional<String>` (empty when `nick` is `null`). Write three methods in `Lookups`:

items: `Optional<String> nickname(Optional<Member> member)` returns the member's nickname upper-cased, or empty.
`Optional<Integer> trimmedLength(Optional<String> text)` returns the length of the trimmed text, or empty when there is no text or nothing is left after trimming.
`<T> T orCreate(Optional<T> value, Supplier<T> factory)` returns the value, or a new one from `factory` when it is missing.

blocks.text: Some members have no nickname, some text is only spaces, and a factory may be costly to call.

cases.says: It upper-cases a nickname, measures trimmed text and keeps a present value.
Member::nickname returns an Optional, so flatMap passes on its emptiness instead of inventing a value.
Text that is blank once trimmed gives an empty Optional, not a length of 0.
The Supplier is called only when the value is missing, as orElseGet does; orElse(factory.get()) calls it every time.

concepts: A reference that returns an Optional belongs in flatMap, or the result nests as Optional<Optional<T>>.
Optional's map and filter take references and pass an empty Optional through untouched.
A Supplier defers its work until get() is called, so a factory handed to orElseGet runs only when the value is missing.
